Both binaries wire the seam: GUI main.rs passes replication_tx + blob_store_for_api, relay main.rs passes repl_tx_for_api (both were already wired at F4). New fe-database/src/replication_mode.rs: ReplicationMode::{Row,Timeseries} with for_table (iot_reading = Timeseries, every other table = Row) - canonical in fe-database because the inbound applier must dispatch on it, re-exported by fe-sync so producers share one definition instead of two that can drift. handlers/replicated_row.rs dispatches per table AFTER the A3 gate (admission precedes mode dispatch, so union semantics never widen authority): Timeseries takes apply_timeseries_row - insert only when the reading_id is absent, never overwrite (a conflicting payload reports Applied with the local value intact, matching the node path whose idempotent re-merge also reports Applied), and an empty Doc::del entry is NotApplicable so a timeseries fact is never tombstoned; Row keeps the tombstone-aware merge. Union semantics are covered at the data layer (fe-database A12 tests: re-delivery idempotent, conflicting payload never overwrites, order-independence, empty entry never removes the fact, viewer denied) and end-to-end by the new harness scenario 10 two_peer_timeseries_sync over the real loopback transport (identical re-delivery stays one row; a conflicting payload does not overwrite; an empty-entry tombstone is NotApplicable with the row still present; an earlier-timestamped reading delivered later still joins the set). REPLY CORRELATION (the F4 handoff hazard): fe-runtime/src/app.rs PendingApiRequests no longer pairs replies FIFO. DbResult carries no correlation id and the DB thread also fans unsolicited results into the same channel (the relay startup scan HierarchyLoaded, GUI hierarchy reloads), so arrival order could cross-pair a racing /ready Ping with a HierarchyLoaded. The queue is now keyed by reply family (ReplyKind) via enqueue_for / reply_kind_of_command / reply_kind_of_result: a result only reaches the oldest waiter of its own family, DbResult::Error is the wildcard delivered to the oldest waiter of any family, and a result with no waiter is dropped rather than mis-delivered. Fire-and-forget commands must not enqueue a waiter - fe-api/src/rest.rs move_waypoint now sends ApiCommand::TransformPersist fire-and-forget (it previously registered a waiter the DB thread never answered, leaving a dangling entry later results could land in). VALIDATED 2026-10-08: F6 (assertions A13+A14) lands the sharded hybrid timeseries fabric. Shard model: ShardId = (petal, anchor node, time bucket) with bucket = recorded_at_ms.div_euclid(bucket_width_ms), epoch-aligned (fe-sync/src/sharding.rs). The shard ledger (__shards/{petal}/{anchor}/{bucket}) and peer capacity declarations (__peers/{did}) ride the verse's own iroh-docs namespace and replicate like any row; a joining peer converges the whole placement picture from the seed_reconciliation snapshot through the same note_* seam the live pump uses. The fabric (VerseFabric: settings + peer declarations + ledger) is SYNC-PLANE state, one entry per open verse in the sync thread's command loop, NOT SurrealDB state: __shards/__peers rows are consumed at the inbound seam (note_entry, BEFORE the own-author filter, so the snapshot re-learns after a restart) and never forwarded to the DB thread. Placement (fe-sync/src/placement.rs) is pure and deterministic (power-of-choices, PROBES=4, candidate sets <= PROBES probed in full, ties break by DID): mirror places every declared peer (capacity hints deliberately do not gate a mode whose point is everyone-holds-everything), sharded places exactly one host, balanced places R hosts with R clamped to the reachable peers (the slider requests, never requires). Seeders are the OVERFLOW tier, never the regular pool (pick_host excludes seeders from the regular branch so a seeder with room stays in reserve; a first-draft defect where the seeder branch was unreachable - seeders were a subset of the eligible pool - was found and fixed, with the new regression test seeders_are_reserved_for_overflow_never_regular_placement); regular capacity exhausted with a seeder roomy = spillover within the seeder's declaration; NO room anywhere = loud least-utilized last resort flagged overflowed, reachable ONLY for a homeless shard (a shard with one host drops extra replica slots honestly - fewer than R - rather than breaking a capacity declaration). A14 holds: the smallest peer never caps the fleet total (a small declaration moves placement to peers with room; only a shard nothing can fit takes the last resort - capacity is a planning hint, not a wall). Settings: canonical TimeseriesMode/VerseTimeseriesSettings in fe-runtime/src/timeseries.rs (lowest common dependency; mirror is the default AND the exact pre-F6 behavior, so an F5-era verse row parses as pure mirror); persisted on the verse row (ts_mode/ts_replication_factor/ts_bucket_width_ms columns, non-optional with DEFAULT mirror/1/86400000); DbCommand::SetVerseTimeseriesSettings (fe-database handlers/verse_settings.rs) sanitizes, persists, replies with the authoritative READ-BACK echo DbResult::VerseTimeseriesSettingsSet, AND re-emits the verse manifest ReplicationEvent carrying the ts_* fields - the manifest doc row IS the replication path for settings (peers' fabrics learn mode/R/bucket from the verse doc row via note_verse_row from BOTH directions of verse-doc traffic: outbound writes parse the manifest before publishing, inbound rows/snapshot replay through note_entry). load_hierarchy surfaces the columns via from_verse_row with clamp-to-default semantics (missing/invalid fields fall back to the mirror defaults - an inbound manifest never fails to converge a fabric over a settings typo). Transfer routing per mode (A13): mirror = Broadcast (all peers), sharded/balanced = Targeted(hosts) - the route is the record the ledger row publishes; on the doc transport every subscriber physically receives the entry, so the route is enforced on the RECEIVE side: retention_decision keeps a reading only when the local peer hosts the shard; an UNKNOWN shard (ledger not converged) retains - the ledger row and the first reading race through the doc, and keep is the safe direction (union semantics make over-retention idempotent; a wrongly-dropped hosted row is data loss). handle_write_row_entry publishes the ledger row BEFORE the reading so the receiver learns the host set first; estimates (row_count/size_bytes) are written once at first sight and tracked locally after (re-publishing per reading would double doc writes for non-authoritative metadata); the host set never re-plans in F6 (membership churn re-planning deferred). Sync commands: SetShardDeclaration (local capacity/seeder, updates every open verse's fabric + republishes __peers/{did}) and GetShardLedger -> SyncEvent::ShardLedger (fabric dump JSON - diagnostics and harness assertions; status.rs drains it).
